[rl-data] Run TaskTrove conversion locally from declared sources (#9970)

Run declared RL sources locally with Zephyr. QUICK downloads pinned
inputs or accepts local files, then stops after the TaskSpec conversion
shared with SAMPLE and FULL. Export tasks as Harbor-compatible TaskTrove
Parquet and bind the RL smoke consumer to it. Builds on #9969; legacy
pipeline deletion is stacked in #9973.

Preserve source actor/grader environments, repository delivery, private
tests, fractional reasoning-gym rewards, structured-output grounding,
and selection tags/modes/language. Keep canonical TaskSpecs independent
of legacy delivery conventions. Verifyit accepts a standalone option
letter or `Answer: D`; prose merely ending in a letter still scores
zero.

The baseline comparison covered all 43 sources and 1,526,908 inputs
against frozen converter `61bb85cc5231d8ac9344696ef51766257940538d`,
using TaskTrove revision `02923004846e4e73862c20962f823a6d05100e7a`.
Comparisons include accept/reject decisions, instructions, private
tests, source/oracle files, permissions, environment recipes and parsed
settings. Subsequent parser, metadata and grader repairs have targeted
follow-up checks; final totals are not a fresh full-corpus census.

Retained conversion differences relative to the frozen converter:

| Source | Accepted difference |
|---|---|
| MCQA | 275 extra exclusions: 216 missing references, 42 conflicting
duplicate-label answers, 17 missing A-starting choice blocks. Final
totals inferred from the baseline and a 971-row repair check: 613,005
accepted / 3,883 rejected. |
| structured | Accept 86 valid schemas corrupted by the old normalizer;
exclude 195 required-but-forbidden and 50 malformed schemas. |
| structured_outputs | Exclude 302 unsatisfiable schemas. |
| IFEval | Exclude 149 prompts with conflicting exclusive-language and
required-word instructions. This is a prompt-consistency policy. |
| Repository tasks | Exclude 32 tasks missing a public submission
path/API contract. |

The 282 reasoning-gym scorer exclusions (#10004), 15 trivial-schema
exclusions and six ARC leak-filter exclusions match legacy behavior.
Bundle checkout Verifyit instead of installing it from Git, and deliver
assistant replies through Harbor answer files.

Harbor Docker execution on one row per source matches frozen rewards
across six sources. MCQA, reasoning-gym, `structured_outputs`, TACO and
SWE-smith pass positive/negative controls. SWE-rebench’s oracle passes
all 34 Elixir tests, but both versions award zero because the archived
parser misses their names (#10003). All sampled environments build and
start; private tests and oracles remain absent before submission. The
`structured_outputs` smoke uses a local stub judge; the pipeline retains
its real grounding judge. Source-wide runtime/dependency equivalence and
judge quality remain unestablished; QUICK skips model review,
release-wide deduplication and release caps.

[ci] Repair native package floor bumps and advance the floors (#9994)

Unit CI on `main` fails in

`test_native_listener_stamps_controller_identity_and_strips_caller_credentials[task]`.
#9818 changed the Rust identity stamping and this test together. Unit CI
on
`main` installs the locked PyPI `marin-iris-native` wheel unless a
change

and sdist counts of the distribution's `ArtifactExpectation`.

The floors advance to `marin-iris-native` 0.1.11.dev37977873285,
`marin-finelog-server` 0.2.54.dev35409391246, and `marin-dupekit-native`
0.1.10.dev36179736977. With these wheels, the iris native proxy tests
and the

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[iris] Take periodic k8s thread dumps without pausing the process (#9998)

`PeriodicProfiler` dumps every running Kubernetes task pod's threads
every 10 minutes. It used py-spy's default `dump`, which stops the
target process while it reads the stacks. In a job whose processes
synchronize frequently, a pause on any process stalls the others. On a
704-GPU training run, each sweep cost 7–10 s of step time, about 1.3% of
throughput.

Periodic dumps now pass `--nonblocking`, so py-spy reads the stacks from
the running process. On one GB200 rack (64 training processes), sweeps
that dumped one pod at a time cost 0.67–0.93 s of step time with
blocking dumps and 0–0.05 s with `--nonblocking`. Scaled to 704
processes, the blocking cost predicts about 9 s per sweep. One of 48
non-blocking pod dumps failed with `Bad address (os error 14)`; the
profiler skips a failed capture for that cycle, as it already does for
any failed dump. On-demand dumps keep pausing for a consistent read.
`build_pyspy_dump_cmd` rejects `--nonblocking` combined with `--native`,
which py-spy 0.4.2 refuses.

The change takes effect when the CoreWeave controller restarts; running
pods need no restart.

[shellbox] Preserve Daytona machines after command timeouts (#9941)

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[iris] Give tasks a token that acts as the job's owner (#9818)

Stacks on #9817.

A controller with auth enabled now mints a control-plane token for each
dispatched task, with the job's owner as subject and the new role
"task". It
rides on RunTaskRequest.task_token, and the Docker worker and the
Kubernetes
pod builder put it in IRIS_TASK_TOKEN for every profile except
CONTAINER_PROFILE_SANDBOX. The in-task client (iris_ctx,
IrisClient.in_cluster,
ClusterResolver) presents it on every controller RPC.

Today a task reaches the controller only through auth.trusted_cidrs,
which
makes it the anonymous admin. On every production cluster tasks share
their
node's address, so those ranges cannot be narrowed while tasks have no
other
credential. With the token, child-job submission, endpoint registration
and
resolution, and ExecInContainer work under the owner's identity.

The task role has no admin authority. A task may give a child job an
elevated
container profile or the PRODUCTION or SYSTEM band only when the child's
parent already holds it, so existing privileged and production job trees
keep
launching children. Raw SQL queries and budget changes fail for a task
that
presents its token, and a root job a task submits is owned by the job's
owner.
Each dispatch mints a fresh token, valid for 30 days and not revocable.
Under
null auth no token is minted. On Kubernetes the token is a plain env
value in
the pod spec, readable by anyone who can read pods in the Iris
namespace.

This change does not narrow auth.trusted_cidrs, so a task that drops its
token
is still the anonymous admin. The proposed per-cluster values are in the
issue,
not in this change; they need this change deployed first, and on GCP and
CoreWeave the node ranges they keep still include every non-sandbox
task.

Part of #9816

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[taskcompendium] Reject unsafe grading artifacts (#9988)

* collect grading artifacts with the task machine's default command
permissions in the shared TaskCompendium grader
* RolloutEngine configures the default command user as the agent's
execution user
  * path substitution cannot grant additional read access
  * source inspection does not provide an atomic filesystem snapshot
* protect the temporary archive path with a root-owned directory that a
non-root agent cannot modify
* reject symlinks in the source path and its ancestors, and included
symlink or hardlink archive members
* limit expanded contents to 1 GiB and 100,000 members per artifact
* these checks run after download and do not limit downloaded bytes or
transfer buffers
* return `SUBMISSION_FAILURE` and zero reward for known invalid or
missing required artifacts
* retain infrastructure errors for archive execution, provider, and host
I/O failures
  * retain the original failure if archive cleanup also fails
* part of #9612

with at most four threads per lookup and writing the verified audit,
accepted rows, and manifest counts in one shard pass. Sample selection
and control trials remain separate executions; trials remain parallel on

executions and a 52.3-second descriptor lookup for ASDiv. The change
reduced verification's median on a local fixture from 1.25 to 0.77

measurement
record](https://loom.oa.dev/s/gslqoxou/artifacts/tuneup-measurements)
describes the fixtures and source telemetry.

Retain the latest 100 finished execution summaries in the Zephyr
dashboard, sort by start time and execution ID, and show the count of
completed stages. Refresh preserves selection, scroll position, and
shard input focus; failed refreshes keep the last snapshot. Retained

and counters are freed.

[rolloutengine] Grade lock-only environments during rollouts (#9967)

Allow RolloutEngine to grade tasks whose grader environment names a
package lock without a Docker image. Curation controls and rollouts
share TaskCompendium's runtime builder, which verifies the lock digest
and builds a managed Python environment with the locked packages,
verifyit, and declared NLTK data.

When LocalMachineFactory is selected, it mounts the built runtime
read-only in each fresh grading sandbox. Runtime preparation remains
within the startup and verifier deadlines, and the attempt owns machine
cleanup. Image-backed graders retain their existing path. Local grading
requires uv, working bubblewrap, and a host process running as root to
stage grader inputs; the local backend does not provide hardware
allocations.

commits.message:
[grug] Let the hero launch use the carry-offload memory budget (#9958)

`trigger_hero.sh` passed `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.75` and
`--xla_gpu_memory_limit_slop_factor=85` to the hero coordinator. Since
#9831, `_apply_hero_ep_runtime_defaults` gives the hero's carry-offload
configuration a 0.78 memory fraction and slop factor 105 together with
`--xla_gpu_enable_host_memory_offloading`. Explicit values take
precedence over those defaults, and `run_grug` copies the coordinator
environment into the training tasks, so a hero launched from main would
compile with 0.75 / 85 and host-memory offloading on. On one GB200 rack
restoring the hero's step-180000 checkpoint, that combination aborts
compilation on every rank in `HloRematerialization`
(`hlo_rematerialization.cc:2118`, `Check failed:
!place_before_list.empty()`).

Without the two overrides the launch resolves to 0.78 / 105 with
host-memory offloading, the configuration measured in the #9831–#9834
rack benchmarks. The live hero is unaffected: Iris retries reuse the
bundle it was launched with.

Follow-up to #9831.

commits.message:
[shellbox] Convert ShellSim panics into command failures (#9965)

Convert ShellSim `SimulationError` from command execution into an exited
command with code 1 and the simulator diagnostic. The reported
piped-stdin generator panic previously escaped both `Machine.run()` and
the persistent Bash session, aborting a Harbor trial; ShellSim 0.1.29
accepts another command after the panic. Apply each interface's output
limit and truncation flag to the diagnostic.

Fixes #9963

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[rl-data] Curate Atlas sources with shared sample-first pipelines (#9798) Add one ingestion point for external RL datasets: every source in the RL Data Atlas is a declaration in `experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/`, and one driver turns the catalog into TaskSpec parquet artifacts with a manifest of what was reviewed, verified and admitted. TaskCompendium supplies the conversion helpers and the pipeline stages; verifyit supplies in-process graders; shellbox runs sandboxed graders. The catalog holds 146 declarations (153 Atlas sources minus seven that exist only as TaskTrove output with no original archive). A declaration states the pinned input, the converter, the agent environment, an optional rubric, optional controls and an optional grader environment: ```python RlDataPipeline( name="math500", source=HfSource("HuggingFaceH4/MATH-500", "6e4ed1a2...", ("test.jsonl",), SourceFormat.JSONL), convert=convert_math500, # (RawRow, ConversionContext) -> TaskSpec | NormalizedTask | ImportRejection version="1", environment=ShellSim(), # or Environment(image="repo@sha256:...") for agentic tasks intended_use=IntendedUse.EVAL, rubric=MATH500_RUBRIC, # optional model review of the source controls=MATH_CONTROLS, # optional grader verification grader=None, # GRADER_PACKAGES or an Environment when a grade script needs packages ) ``` Each source runs the same stages. The rubric decides the source once from a fixed panel of up to 100 rows; rows outside the panel are never reviewed individually. Controls grade one known submission per sampled task, the golden when the declaration has one or an empty submission otherwise, and reject the source when the grader does not behave. ```mermaid flowchart LR D[download
pinned files] --> N[normalize
convert rows to TaskSpec] N --> P[quality panel
up to 100 rows, rubric review] P -->|defects > 50%| R[gated: source rejected] P -->|reviews missing and
could still reject| I[incomplete: resume] P -->|otherwise trusted| F[filter
panel rows by their review,
other rows inherit the decision] F --> V[verify
controls on 20 sampled tasks] V -->|pass rate < 95%| R2[gated: grader rejected] V -->|pass| E[export
final/ rows with a ready grader] E --> M[manifest.json
counts, reports, admission] ``` The driver runs in `sample` or `full` mode. A full run is the real thing: it converts every row, draws its own panel and control sample, and gates the source on its own evidence. A sample run is a test of a declaration: it converts and gates only the panel and leaves the other rows unprocessed with the gate's reason. Nothing is inherited between runs; sources are independent artifacts and a campaign is just a set of them sharing one worker pool. ```mermaid flowchart LR DL["task-curation/download/<hash>"] --> S["data/rl/<name>-<hash>
mode=sample (test)"] DL --> Fu["data/rl/<name>-<hash>
mode=full"] ENV["images/env-<id>
grader lock or image"] --> S ENV --> Fu ``` Graders are placed by what they need. A grader with no environment runs in process through verifyit. A grader that declares packages runs in a sandbox chosen from the declaration: a digest-pinned image runs as an Iris task under gVisor; apt packages the worker image lacks run in an image built for the environment; everything else, including the shared `GRADER_PACKAGES`, runs in a bubblewrap sandbox on the Zephyr worker over a self-contained Python environment that shellbox builds once per worker from the environment's hash lock (a uv-managed CPython and a venv under one root, mounted read-only). Workers therefore run with the privileged container profile. Grading machines never have network access. ```mermaid flowchart TD G[grader] -->|no environment| IP[in process: verifyit] G -->|image digest| IR[Iris task, gVisor sandbox] G -->|apt beyond the worker image| BI[built image, Iris task] G -->|pypi lock only| BW[bubblewrap on the Zephyr worker
uv-built CPython + venv root, read-only] ``` One Iris driver job runs the whole campaign. It keeps one Zephyr worker pool for every source, admits a bounded number of sources at a time, and writes a campaign report with each source's outcome as it finishes. Reviews go to the GLM relay through a request cache keyed by the exact request and model revision, so a rebuilt artifact does not repeat identical inference. ```mermaid flowchart LR H[iris hub] --> J[driver job on a federation cluster] J --> Z[Zephyr pool
N privileged workers] J --> C[campaign report] Z --> G1[review: GLM relay + cache] Z --> G2[graders: in process / bubblewrap] Z --> G3[graders: Iris tasks with images] ``` Each source artifact contains: | Path | Contents | |---|---| | `download/` | Row locators of the staged files and the input identity | | `normalize/` | Every converted row: TaskSpec JSON or a typed rejection | | `review/` | Panel reviews, filter decisions, unprocessed rows, the quality report | | `verify/` | Sampled controls, trials and the source verification decision | | `final/` | Admitted rows: kept, with a ready grader, source verified where required | | `manifest.json`, `telemetry.json` | Status, counts, reports, admission, execution timings | TaskSpec gains a typed `grader` union (`VerifyitGrader`, `ScriptGrader`, `SessionGrader`, `NoGrader`) and `answer_format` in place of the string verifier kind, and one grading implementation is shared by the pipeline's controls and rolloutengine. Script graders print their reward as the last non-empty stdout line; vendored upstream scorers are shipped byte for byte next to each declaration. Sampled over the whole catalog, 131 sources end `sampled`, six are gated by their panel or controls (hardmath, taco, pymethods, unitsyn and their large variants) and the ARC inductive sources need a follow-up on their scorer. A full run over five trial sources (math500, rlvr_ifeval, tasktrove-calendar, tasktrove-nl2bash and the Nemotron STEM MCQA source) completed every source: 21,767 rows converted, all five panels trusted and all five control suites passed, with only the 100-row panel of each source reviewed. Judge-graded sources reach `final/` without controls until a judge control exists; sources with no controls stay out of `final/` when their grader runs in a sandbox. Follow-ups are tracked in #9943, #9944, #9945 and #9946. --------- Co-authored-by: rjpower
